ai.description: This small frog reaches 20–25 mm. It is brownish-grey with a pale mid-dorsal stripe and dark flank markings. A distinctive feature is the presence of a prominent papilla on the tongue.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Liurana himalayana* is best distinguished by the presence of a distinct, fleshy papilla on the center of its tongue, a feature absent in other similar Indian frog species.
ai.habitat: *Liurana himalayana* inhabits high-altitude moist temperate forests and alpine meadows in the Himalayas, typically found near streams at elevations between 2,500 and 4,000m.
ai.behavior: The Himalayan Papilla-tongued Frog is primarily nocturnal, emerging at night to forage for small invertebrates along the moist, rocky banks of high-altitude streams.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Liurana himalayana* breeds during the monsoon (June–August). It is an oviparous species that lays small clutches of large, unpigmented eggs in high-altitude rock crevices.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Liurana himalayana* is found in the Eastern Himalayas of Arunachal Pradesh, India, typically inhabiting high-altitude streams between 2,500 and 3,500 meters.
ai.callDescription: The advertisement call of *Liurana himalayana* consists of a series of high-pitched, pulsed notes emitted from within moist, rocky crevices near high-altitude streams.
